title: OIDC DPoP — Demonstrating Proof of Possession
subtitle: Bind the access token to a key the client holds, so a stolen token is useless without a matching per-request proof JWT (RFC 9449).

steps.label: Generate key pair + build token proof
steps.lede: The public client generates a DPoP key pair (the private key never leaves the app) and builds a proof JWT for the token request: header carries the public jwk and typ dpop+jwt, payload binds the HTTP method and URL.

jwt.title: DPoP proof for POST /token
payload: Unique id — server tracks it to block replay
Must equal the request URI (no query)
Issued-at — tight freshness window; no ath yet

steps.devtools: Not a network event. The jwk in the header is the PUBLIC key only — the AS will hash it to derive the binding thumbprint. There is no ath claim here: there's no access token to hash yet.

steps.label: POST /token with DPoP proof
steps.lede: The client redeems its authorization code (PKCE underneath) and attaches the proof in the DPoP request header. The AS verifies the proof and computes the key thumbprint.
steps.devtools: In the Network tab, filter on /token and read the DPoP request header. Split it on . and base64url-decode header + payload: confirm typ=dpop+jwt, an asymmetric alg (ES256), the jwk, and htm=POST / htu matching this request.

steps.label: 200 DPoP-bound token
steps.lede: The AS returns token_type DPoP (not Bearer) and binds the access token to the proof's key via cnf.jkt — the SHA-256 thumbprint of the jwk.
steps.devtools: token_type is DPoP, not Bearer — the client must present it with the DPoP scheme from now on. The token is bound via cnf.jkt = "0ZcOCORZNYy-DWpqq30jZyJGHTN0d2HglBV3uiguA4I", the SHA-256 thumbprint of the step-1 jwk. For an opaque token you'd see jkt via introspection; for a JWT AT it's in the payload's cnf.

steps.label: Build resource proof with ath
steps.lede: For the API call the client builds a NEW proof — same key, but a fresh jti and iat, htm/htu for the resource, and an ath claim that hashes the access token.

jwt.title: DPoP proof for GET /resource
payload: DIFFERENT jti from the token-endpoint proof

steps.devtools: Verify ath by hand: printf %s "mF_9.B5f-4.1JqM" | openssl dgst -binary -sha256 | basenc --base64url and compare. The jti must be new — never reuse the step-1 value.

steps.label: GET /resource with DPoP scheme + proof
steps.lede: The client calls the API presenting the token with the DPoP auth scheme (not Bearer) and the fresh proof. The API verifies everything in one shot.
steps.devtools: Note the DPoP auth scheme, not Bearer. The API verifies: (1) proof signature against the embedded jwk, (2) jkt(jwk) == the token's cnf.jkt, (3) ath == hash(token), (4) htm/htu match, (5) jti fresh. A bound token replayed as plain Bearer, or a proof signed by a different key, fails checks 1/2 → 401 invalid_token.

steps.label: Nonce challenge → retry
steps.lede: When the server requires a DPoP nonce, a proof without one is rejected 400 use_dpop_nonce with a DPoP-Nonce header. The client copies that value into a nonce claim on a rebuilt proof and retries, which then succeeds.
steps.devtools: Read the DPoP-Nonce response header (WWW-Authenticate: DPoP … at the resource server). Add it as a nonce claim to the next proof and retry — you'll see the failed attempt immediately followed by a 200. This closes the pre-generated-proof gap. A reused jti within the server's window also yields 401 invalid_token.
